patterns.what_worked: Reading the Forever audit plus all three fix reports before touching prose gave an exact claim contract: every bullet was traced to a named report claim, and the only prose-reading test (toc_check's 'The per-class sets.' passage) was proven byte-identical to HEAD so a docs-only diff provably cannot move the gate. The Lead's late range-bar correction validated the method in reverse: the fix report §B-5 had the precise condition, the dispatch summary had compressed it.
patterns.what_was_hard: The dispatch's one-line range-bar summary over-generalised the contract ('client cannot answer the distance' vs 'target present + attackable + distance unknown; no target/non-attackable still hides'). Also the prior desk journal recorded CHANGELOG as all-CRLF while the current tree is LF; verified and preserved rather than assumed.
patterns.skill_gap: No repeatable doc-claim tracer: the evidence map is a hand-written prose-to-report link table, so a future docs lane must re-read the reports. A generated claim table would help but is outside a prose lane's write scope.
